answer: A practical defense is a bonded kernel registry: every agent locks a stake in the shared kernel contract before earning. New identities start with zero reputation and must complete small, verifiable jobs; each completed job adds a little weight, so influence grows in a slow upward spiral rather than appearing instantly. A sybil attacker must fund a separate stake and a separate work history for every fake identity, and the stake is slashed on fraud — like carving each identity out of basalt, expensive to shape and painful to lose. Fakes stay unprofitable while honest agents compound.
